tasks.short: Pick metals, glass, wood, paper and plastics from the line or floor and drop each into the right container.

steps.what: Sorter picks items from the conveyor and identifies the materials
Sorter drops each item into the right container or bunker
Sorter checks the wall chart or asks the shift lead about unknown items
Sorter radios the loader driver when a container is full
Loader driver swaps the full container for an empty one
Shift lead spot-checks container purity and tells sorters about contamination

tasks.design: Fill-level sensors on containers send a swap request to the loader driver's terminal through the {OPS_SYSTEM}, and a picture-based sorting guide on a station tablet ({DOCS}) answers 'where does this go'. The shift lead records purity checks per line on the same tablet; picking and dropping stay manual unless the site invests in optical sorters.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sorting is physical judgement, and sensors and tablets on a dusty line were not worth the trouble.
tasks.enabler_now: Low-cost fill-level sensors and rugged tablets are common, and a picture guide is a simple records app.
tasks.still_hard: Identifying and picking items stays hands-on; optical and robotic sorters need capital spend and are not assumed.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising odd or dangerous items, such as batteries or gas canisters, before they reach the wrong stream.

ambition.what: Purity per line reviewed every shift, so contamination is fixed before a load is rejected.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; fewer radio calls and look-ups during the shift.

reach.learn: Whether the same picture guide helps collectors explain rejections.

evidence.claim: Container fill-level sensors can send swap requests to an operations system.
Optical sorters exist for paper, plastics and metals but need capital investment.
Separate collection and recycling targets come from EU waste law; acceptance rules for each stream follow national rules and buyer specifications.

assumptions: Boundary: from items on the line to full containers swapped; baling and sale are outside.
Input contract: container ID, fraction and fill level from the sensor; picture guide items maintained by the shift lead; fallback is the radio and wall chart.
Loader driver and shift lead time is outside the sorter's savings.
Purity is recorded per line, not per person.
unknowns: How many containers and fractions each station serves.
Whether the site has network coverage on the sorting floor.
research_questions: How often are loads downgraded for contamination today?

already_counted.description: Sorter still identifies and drops every item.

incremental.description: Sorter cleans or reports blocked sensors.
Shift lead keeps the picture guide current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Lines where containers are swapped on a fixed schedule save little on radio calls, and picking is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Separate scrap into copper, brass, aluminium and other high-grade metals, testing doubtful pieces.

steps.what: Sorter inspects scrap metals by colour, weight and magnet test
Sorter tests doubtful pieces with the handheld alloy analyser
Sorter places pieces in copper, brass, aluminium or stainless bins
Sorter writes analyser readings and bin number on a paper sheet
Yard supervisor checks bin grades before sale and downgrades mixed bins
Sorter tells the weighbridge a bin is full and ready to weigh

tasks.design: The handheld analyser sends each reading to a yard app in the {OPS_SYSTEM} after the sorter scans the bin ID, so readings and bin grades are logged without paper; a full-bin button notifies the weighbridge. The yard supervisor sees readings per bin before sale, and the same log produces a grade sheet for the buyer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Analyser readings stayed on the device or on paper, and nobody linked them to bins.
tasks.enabler_now: Many handheld analysers export readings over a cable or wireless link, and a bin-scan app is a small records build.
tasks.still_hard: Sorting by eye and hand is the work; scrap prices reward speed more than records.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising alloys by feel and look and spotting coated or mixed pieces that fool a quick test.

ambition.what: A grade sheet per bin, built from logged readings, that buyers can trust for a better price.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; the sorter stops writing readings down.

reach.role: laborer and freight, stock and material mover
reach.learn: Whether bin IDs and grades can drive the loading list.

evidence.claim: Handheld alloy analysers can export readings to other systems.
A scan at each handling step can write the record in the stock system, with coded reasons instead of paper tallies.

assumptions: Boundary: from mixed scrap to graded bins ready to weigh; sale and pricing are outside.
Input contract: analyser reading with alloy and composition, bin ID label, produced by the analyser and bin labels; fallback is the paper sheet.
Yard supervisor time is outside the sorter's savings.
Sorting and testing time do not change.
unknowns: Whether the site's analysers can export readings.
Whether buyers pay more for documented grades.
research_questions: How often are bins downgraded by buyers today?

already_counted.description: Sorter still inspects, tests and places every piece.

incremental.description: Sorter rescans bins when a reading fails to transfer.
Yard supervisor keeps bin labels and grade lists current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Yards that test few pieces with the analyser log little today, and the weighbridge call saving disappears where bins are weighed on a fixed round.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect construction debris on site and sort concrete, gypsum, wood, plastics and metal into containers.

steps.what: Recycling worker collects debris around the construction site
Recycling worker sorts construction materials into stone, wood, gypsum, plastics and metal containers
Recycling worker checks container signs or asks the site lead about mixed items
Recycling worker phones the site office when a container is full
Site office checks the request and agrees the container swap
Site office books the container exchange with the waste hauler
Waste hauler swaps the container and issues a weigh ticket

tasks.design: Each container carries a QR code that opens a picture guide of what goes in and what does not ({DOCS}) and a 'full' button with photo. The request goes to the site office in a {WORKFLOW} app; once the office approves, the booking goes to the hauler through the {PARTNER_PORTAL} or {EMAIL}, and the weigh ticket is attached to the same record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site waste was handled by phone and paper because each site is temporary.
tasks.enabler_now: QR codes and a form app take a day to set up per site, and haulers increasingly take bookings online.
tasks.still_hard: Collecting and sorting debris is physical; mixed demolition waste resists clean separation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising asbestos-suspect or contaminated material and stopping before it is mixed in.

ambition.what: Weekly separation rates per site from weigh tickets, so site managers see their recycling share during the project.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; fewer calls to the office.

reach.task: Throw site waste in the right container
reach.learn: Whether the QR picture guide reduces mixed containers.

evidence.claim: A QR code on a container can open a picture guide and a request form.
Separation of construction and demolition waste on site and suspected asbestos handling follow national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from debris on site to containers swapped; processing at the recycler is outside.
Input contract: container ID, fraction, site and hauler, produced by the site office when the container arrives; fallback is a phone call.
Site office and hauler time is outside the recycling worker's savings.
unknowns: Whether the hauler accepts online bookings.
How many fractions each site separates.
research_questions: Does a picture guide on containers cut mixed loads charged at a higher rate?

already_counted.description: Recycling worker still collects and sorts all debris.

incremental.description: Recycling worker replaces damaged QR labels.
Site office sets up containers and guides per site.

approvals.approved_version: Swap request for one container ID with fraction and photo as approved in s5; a changed request needs a new approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Small sites with one or two containers rarely call for swaps, and collecting and sorting do not change.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Weigh and log recycled materials and hazardous parts removed from products, label containers, hand logs on.

steps.what: Dismantler weighs removed hazardous parts and material fractions on the scale
Dismantler looks up the waste code for unusual chemicals in the code list
Dismantler writes weight, material, waste code and container number in the paper log
Dismantler hand-writes hazardous container labels with content, code and date
Shift lead checks the shift's log entries and signs them
Office administrator keys signed logs into the waste register spreadsheet
Environmental coordinator compiles and files the waste report on the government portal

tasks.design: A tablet app at the scale, built on the {OPS_SYSTEM} or a {WORKFLOW} form: the dismantler scans the container ID and picks the material, which carries its waste code; the connected scale sends the weight and a printer issues the hazardous label. The shift lead approves the shift's entries on the tablet, approved entries flow into the waste register on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, and the coordinator reviews a generated period report before filing it on the {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scales, labels and the register were separate, so every weight was written, signed, keyed and re-added by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Scales with data output, label printers and form apps are cheap, and a register table can generate the period report.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual chemicals still need a person to classify; regulators' portals may accept only manual entry or fixed file formats.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a part that leaks or contains something not on the list, and stopping to classify it safely.

ambition.what: Monthly mass balance per waste stream checked against intake, instead of once a year at audit.

tasks.altitude: The dismantler scans and checks instead of writing; the shift lead approves on a tablet and the coordinator reviews rather than compiles.

reach.task: Record removed asbestos or chemicals before transport
reach.learn: Whether the same scan, weigh and label flow fits their containers.

evidence.claim: A scan at each handling step can write the record, with coded reasons replacing paper tallies.
Holders of hazardous waste must keep chronological records of quantity, nature and destination under EU waste law; reporting formats follow national rules.
In the Netherlands, scanners that log each action per person can observe performance, so the works council must consent.
A French regulator fined a logistics operator for per-person scanner indicators and long retention.

assumptions: Boundary: from removed parts on the scale to the period report filed; dismantling itself and transport are outside.
Input contract: material list with waste code and label text, maintained by the environmental coordinator; container ID labels; weight from the scale; fallback is the paper log.
Entries carry the user for traceability but are not used to score people.
Shift lead, office administrator and coordinator time is outside the dismantler's savings.
unknowns: Whether the scale has a data output.
Which formats the authority's portal accepts.
research_questions: How many log errors are found at audit today?

already_counted.description: Dismantler checks the scanned entry before saving.

incremental.description: Dismantler handles printer and scale faults and uses paper when the tablet is down.
Environmental coordinator keeps the material list, codes and label texts current.

approvals.approved_version: The shift's log entries as approved by the shift lead in s5; a later correction reopens approval.
Period report file generated from approved register entries, as reviewed by the coordinator before filing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Sites with many unusual items keep looking up codes, and scales without data output keep manual weight entry.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The worker keeps the physical sorting and judgement; radio calls, paper logs and hand-written labels shrink.
skills_to_grow: Recording materials accurately with scans and codes
Using a picture guide and keeping it honest
role.ambitious_version: A recycling worker whose scans and logs give buyers trusted grade sheets and the site a monthly mass balance, with no paper in between.
